Paint the Joker from Batman. He is sitting alone in an empty theatre box after the show, a pale face, swept green hair and sardonic red smile, wearing an elegant violet suit with a green waistcoat. He balances a delicate white teacup on its saucer with both hands, looking toward the empty stage with an amused, unreadable expression. Slightly elevated three-quarter viewpoint, tall angular silhouette curled into a velvet seat. A narrow warm stage light grazes his cheek; deep muted burgundy curtain and blue shadow behind. The focus is theatrical personality, fine cloth and the fragile cup.

Paint the Penguin, Oswald Cobblepot from Batman. A short, stocky middle-aged man with a hooked nose, monocle, black formal suit and ivory waistcoat, sitting behind a dark wooden desk in a harbor-side office. His top hat rests visibly on the desk. He leans forward, carefully moving one black king on a small chessboard with a gloved hand, his other hand resting on the desk edge, watching his move with sharp calculating eyes. His closed umbrella rests against the side of the chair. Soft gray daylight from a tall window, one distant ship shape in mist, sparse room. Warm brass, rich black fabric and weathered wood, precise painted expression.
